name: Palmieri ESWT
question: Does focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy improve symptoms or penile deformity compared with sham treatment in Peyronie's disease?

arms.label: sham treatment with a nonfunctioning transducer

design.population: 100 men with Peyronie's disease of no more than 12 months' duration and no prior Peyronie's-related treatment.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and methods, pp 364–365; Results, Table 2, p 365; corrigendum, p e43

verdictNote: Pain, erectile-function and quality-of-life scores improved; plaque size and curvature did not improve significantly.
takeaway: In 100 men randomized to four weekly focused shock wave or sham sessions, pain had resolved 12 weeks after the last session in 23/43 versus 3/42 men with baseline pain; erectile-function and quality-of-life scores favored treatment, while plaque size and curvature did not improve significantly.

reports.label: Randomized trial
reports.citation: Palmieri A, Imbimbo C, Longo N, et al. "A First Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial Evaluating Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for the Treatment of Peyronie's Disease." *Eur Urol.* 2009;56(2):363-370. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2009.05.012
reports.followUp: 12 and 24 weeks after the final treatment session
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and methods, p 365

results.measure: Pain during erection, 0–10 VAS; pain resolution among men with baseline pain at 12 weeks; mean VAS at 12 and 24 weeks after treatment

values.exp: Baseline mean VAS 5.19; pain resolved in 23/43 at 12 weeks; mean VAS lower than baseline and sham at 12 weeks (p<0.001); lower than baseline, 12 weeks and sham at 24 weeks (p<0.001 for between-group comparison)
values.ctl: Baseline mean VAS 5.51; pain resolved in 3/42 at 12 weeks; mean VAS not significantly changed at 12 weeks; lower than baseline and 12 weeks at 24 weeks

results.note: No numeric follow-up means or between-arm effect estimate are printed in the supplied full-text extraction; the paper designates objective and subjective outcome measures but no primary endpoint.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 365; Results 3.2.1–3.2.2 and Fig. 2, pp 366–367; corrigendum, p e43

results.measure: Mean IIEF-5 and number without erectile dysfunction at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks after treatment

values.exp: Baseline mean IIEF-5 14.00; no ED in 4/50 at baseline, 25/50 at 12 weeks and 27/50 at 24 weeks; mean score improved from baseline at 12 weeks (p<0.001) and remained stable at 24 weeks
values.ctl: Baseline mean IIEF-5 14.16; no ED in 3/50 at baseline, 0/50 at 12 weeks and 1/50 at 24 weeks; mean score not significantly changed from baseline

results.note: Between-group mean IIEF-5 differences were significant at 12 and 24 weeks (p<0.001); no numeric follow-up means or effect estimate are printed in the supplied extraction.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 365; Fig. 3 and Table 3, p 366; Results 3.2.1–3.2.2, pp 366–367

results.measure: Mean study-specific 0–25 quality-of-life score at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks after treatment; higher score indicates better quality of life

values.exp: Baseline mean 16.6; increased from baseline at 12 weeks (p<0.001); remained higher than sham at 24 weeks (p<0.001)
values.ctl: Baseline mean 17.52; no significant change at 12 weeks; increased from baseline at 24 weeks

results.note: The questionnaire was not validated. The corrigendum reverses the original Table 1 item-score order; higher total scores indicate better quality of life. No numeric follow-up means or effect estimate are printed in the supplied extraction.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 365; Fig. 4 and Results 3.2.1–3.2.2, pp 366–367; corrigendum, Tables 1–2, pp e43–e44

results.measure: Mean plaque area in cm² at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks after treatment

values.exp: Baseline mean 1.50 cm²; decreased nonsignificantly from baseline at 12 and 24 weeks
values.ctl: Baseline mean 1.59 cm²; increased nonsignificantly at 12 weeks; higher than baseline and ESWT at 24 weeks (p<0.05)

results.note: Corrected baseline means are from the corrigendum; no numeric follow-up means or effect estimate are printed in the supplied extraction.
results.locator: Full text, Fig. 5 and Results 3.2.1–3.2.2, pp 366–367; corrigendum, Table 2 correction, p e43

results.measure: Mean penile curvature in degrees among 44 men with recurvatum per arm at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks after treatment

values.exp: Baseline mean 28.88° (n=44); decreased nonsignificantly from baseline at 12 and 24 weeks
values.ctl: Baseline mean 29.45° (n=44); increased nonsignificantly at 12 weeks; higher than baseline and ESWT at 24 weeks (p<0.05)

results.note: No numeric follow-up means or effect estimate are printed in the supplied extraction.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 365; Fig. 6 and Results 3.2.1–3.2.2, pp 366–367

results.endpoint: Would recommend treatment to a friend
results.measure: Yes response at 24 weeks, randomized men
results.note: No between-group test reported; other responses were 5 no and 10 don't know with ESWT, and 29 no and 12 don't know with sham.

harms.label: Major complications and analgesic use during treatment

values.exp: No major complications; 0/50 needed analgesics during treatment

delivery.label: Active treatment
delivery.value: Four weekly sessions, each delivering 2,000 focused shock waves
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and methods, p 365

delivery.label: Sham treatment
delivery.value: Four weekly sessions with a nonfunctioning transducer
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and methods, p 365

delivery.label: Device, dose and procedure
delivery.value: Storz Duolith; 2,000 impulses per session at 0.25 mJ/mm² and 4 Hz; static energy focus, manually operated probe; four consecutive weekly sessions without anesthesia
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and methods and Fig. 1, p 365; Discussion, p 368

values.exp: 50/50 completed all sessions and 12- and 24-week follow-up
values.ctl: 50/50 completed all sessions and 12- and 24-week follow-up
